question.problem:
Which of the diagrams below shows three collinear points?

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14134102/assets/c0df27c96da9f9c285438faee93652f81362fe91a51dc28e02ec0e2e9ff42177.png)
question.worked_solution:
Three (or more) points are collinear if a straight line passes through all points.

With that in mind, let's examine our diagrams in turn.

- Diagram I shows three points that are *not* collinear. We can't draw a straight line that passes through all three points.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14134102/assets/4967d8325f8ed8415a8404286d29ff97eb65cd6926ed1ca27a943178aee1a3cc.png)

- Diagram II shows three collinear points. There is a straight line that passes through all three of these points.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14134102/assets/af746af6fba54f69570f5dcfa38fbbb4cffd290080cc45deec433bc5266aa75e.png)

- Diagram III shows three points that are *not* collinear. We can't draw a straight line that passes through all three points.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14134102/assets/c0d9d178c5be09aa7f6ad1927c6f8e930154cf077aabbd18a765820babd63069.png)

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."
